scope.flow: Order posting validation for non-post-only orders in the CLOB contract, specifically the zero-cost trade check using bitwise '&'

statements.text: A user posts an order that is not post-only.
For the order, the amounts received and sent are not the same.
The zero-cost trade check uses bitwise operator '&' to ensure one of the values is not zero, but '&' can return zero for properly calculated nonzero values.
A non-post-only order whose received and sent amounts are not the same and which is not a zero-cost trade should not be reverted by the zero-cost check.
Denial of services where orders that should succeed are reverted.

ambiguities: No explicit attacker action or unauthorized caller is described; the report describes a validation logic flaw affecting legitimate orders.
The report does not give concrete numeric values for the amounts that trigger the '&' false-zero result.
The report does not specify whether the revert occurs at order posting time or a later matching step beyond the cited check.
